newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rise in active trade by break.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rise in active trade by break.

text.p: Battered Thai stocks, which fell to new eight-year lows last Friday, recovered slightly in active trade by the lunch break on Monday on advance of blue-chip stocks, brokers said.
"Local investors and mutual funds were active. Their buying was aimed at squaring positions after local and foreign sales on Friday," said a broker at Securities One.
The SET index rose 3.48 points to 534.10 on 5.7 billion baht turnover by lunch. The indicator was off its morning high of 542.08.
Brokers said they saw no tangible positive news to back the buying in the morning and most foreign investors remained on the sidelines on worries about the weak economy.
Most key sectors advanced. Banks topped the active list, gaining 2.26 percent and the finance sector advanced 0.48 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, rising two baht to 95, and BEC World shed four to 212.
